WITH project_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    sp.arcref,
    p.fundflux,
    CASE 
      WHEN SUM(sp.boxz) > 0 
      THEN SUM(sp.boxx) / SUM(sp.boxz)
      ELSE NULL 
    END as ratio
  FROM scanspatial sp
  INNER JOIN projects p ON sp.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY sp.arcref, p.fundflux
),
with_excess AS (
  SELECT 
    arcref,
    fundflux,
    ratio,
    ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY fundflux) as excess
  FROM project_ratios
)
SELECT 
  arcref,
  fundflux,
  ratio,
  excess
FROM with_excess
WHERE excess > 0
ORDER BY excess DESC
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: "Ignoring missing ones" when summing boxx and boxz means NULL values are omitted from SUM() operations, per standard SQL behavior

"Whose ratio is above their funding source's average by the most" means projects where excess > 0 (ratio exceeds the funding source average), returned in descending order by excess magnitude, with fewer than 10 rows possible if fewer than 10 projects exceed their source's average

alternatives.interpretation: Include all projects (both above and below funding source average), sorting the 10 highest by excess (descending), with NULL excess values appearing last. This would accommodate the "missing values last" phrase if it refers to projects with NULL ratios.
